screen1-a1.glyph: three horizontal lines of decreasing length
screen1-a1.description: three stacked lines control in the top-left corner of the toolbar
screen1-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Open menu" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen1-a1.convention_relied_on: three stacked horizontal lines (hamburger) is an established convention for opening the app's navigation menu — my reading, confidence high
screen1-a1.initial_rationale: unlabeled, but the hamburger glyph is a widely-known convention; common-icon exemption applies pending the behavioural test

test_cases.expected_result: a navigation panel slides in from the left
test_cases.confirms_if: it does something other than open a navigation menu
test_cases.overturns_if: a navigation menu opens, matching the convention
test_cases.observed_result: a side panel slid in from the left listing Chats, Projects, Code, Artifacts, recent chats and a New chat button

screen1-a1.deciding_evidence: tapping the hamburger opened the side navigation panel, exactly what the convention promises

screen1-a2.glyph: ghost outline with two dots for eyes
screen1-a2.description: ghost outline glyph in the top-right corner of the toolbar
screen1-a2.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Incognito chat" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen1-a2.convention_relied_on: a ghost outline is not an established mobile convention; I know of no common meaning a first-time user could rely on — my reading, confidence high that it is not a convention
screen1-a2.initial_rationale: no visible text anywhere near it and the ghost is not a recognizable convention; nothing on the screen says what it does

test_cases.action: long-press the ghost glyph to look for a tooltip or label
test_cases.expected_result: no tooltip; any label that appears would overturn the verdict
test_cases.confirms_if: no tooltip or visible label appears before or during the press
test_cases.overturns_if: a tooltip or visible caption names the control
test_cases.observed_result: no tooltip appeared; the long-press acted as a tap and switched the screen into incognito mode

test_cases.precondition: home screen, normal chat, nothing typed
test_cases.action: check the toolbar row and the surrounding screen for any copy belonging to the glyph, then tap it
test_cases.expected_result: no copy before the tap; the purpose becomes visible only after acting
test_cases.confirms_if: the only explanation appears after the tap
test_cases.overturns_if: an explanatory caption is visible before tapping
test_cases.observed_result: nothing on the home screen refers to the glyph; only after tapping did the words 'Incognito chat' and 'Incognito chats stay out of your history and search, and aren't used to train Claude.' appear, and the glyph changed to an X

screen1-a2.deciding_evidence: no label, tooltip or adjacent copy exists before the tap, and the ghost glyph is not a convention; the explanation is shown only after the user has already switched modes
screen1-a2.recommendation: put a visible word beside or under the glyph, e.g. 'Incognito' (or 'Private chat'), so the mode is named before it is switched on

screen1-a3.description: 'Upgrade to Pro' link at the right of the grey banner above the typing box
screen1-a3.visible_text: "Upgrade to Pro" beside the banner text "Get more with Claude Pro"
screen1-a3.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Upgrade to Pro" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen1-a3.initial_rationale: explicit verb and object; a first-time user can tell it leads to upgrading to a paid Pro plan

test_cases.action: tap 'Upgrade to Pro' and observe (nothing confirmed)
test_cases.confirms_if: something other than an upgrade offer opens
test_cases.observed_result: a full-height sheet titled 'Get more Claude — Choose the plan right for you' opened with Pro and Max price options; closed it with its X without selecting anything

screen1-a3.deciding_evidence: the link opened the plan screen it names

screen1-a4.description: text entry box at the bottom of the screen
screen1-a4.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Chat with Claude…" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen1-a4.initial_rationale: placeholder names what goes in (a chat message to Claude); no format or constraint matters for free text

test_cases.action: tap the box and type 'hello' (not sent)
test_cases.expected_result: text accepted; the purpose stays evident once typing starts
test_cases.confirms_if: the hint vanishes on focus with nothing to replace it
test_cases.overturns_if: the hint survives focus and the typed text itself is the message
test_cases.observed_result: on focus the placeholder stayed visible with the cursor; it disappeared only once 'hello' was typed, and a send arrow replaced the right-hand round button; text deleted without sending

screen1-a4.deciding_evidence: the placeholder survives focus and names the job; it is replaced only by the user's own message, with a send arrow appearing

screen1-a5.glyph: plus sign in a grey circle
screen1-a5.description: plus sign in a grey circle at the left of the typing bar
screen1-a5.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Add to chat" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen1-a5.convention_relied_on: a plus in a message composer is an established 'add/attach' convention — my reading, confidence high
screen1-a5.initial_rationale: unlabeled plus in the composer toolbar; add/attach convention; exemption pending the behavioural test

test_cases.expected_result: a panel for adding things to the chat opens
test_cases.confirms_if: it does something other than add/attach
test_cases.observed_result: a bottom sheet titled 'Add to chat' opened with Camera, Photos, Files, Add to project, Web search, Connectors (and, live, a Memory switch)

screen1-a5.deciding_evidence: the plus opened the 'Add to chat' sheet, as the add convention promises

screen1-a6.description: pill in the typing bar with the words 'Haiku 4.5'
screen1-a6.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Haiku 4.5" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen1-a6.initial_rationale: the pill shows a proper name and a version number; nothing says it is a model, or that pressing it lets you change which one answers — a first-time user has no way to read 'Haiku 4.5' as a setting

test_cases.expected_result: if the label conveyed its purpose, the result would be predictable from 'Haiku 4.5'
test_cases.confirms_if: what opens is something the words 'Haiku 4.5' did not predict
test_cases.overturns_if: the pill itself says what it controls, or the result is obvious from it
test_cases.observed_result: a sheet titled 'Select model' opened listing Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku with descriptions; only after opening did the word 'model' appear anywhere

screen1-a6.deciding_evidence: the purpose ('choose the model') is disclosed only by the sheet the tap opens; the pill's face is a product name a first-time user cannot interpret
screen1-a6.recommendation: show the purpose on the pill, e.g. 'Model: Haiku 4.5 ▾', or a caption 'Choose model'

screen1-a7.glyph: microphone outline in a grey circle
screen1-a7.description: microphone outline in a grey circle, second from the right in the typing bar
screen1-a7.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Start speech input" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen1-a7.convention_relied_on: a microphone is an established 'speak / dictate' convention — my reading, confidence high
screen1-a7.initial_rationale: unlabeled microphone in a text composer; dictation convention; exemption pending the behavioural test

test_cases.confirms_if: it starts something other than speech input
test_cases.observed_result: a full-height sheet opened: 'Send messages to Claude using your voice.' with a language picker and Continue; closed it with its X before any permission prompt

screen1-a7.deciding_evidence: the microphone opened a voice-dictation intro, matching the convention

screen1-a8.glyph: white vertical bars of varying height in a black circle
screen1-a8.description: round black button with white vertical bars at the right end of the typing bar
screen1-a8.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Voice Mode" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen1-a8.convention_relied_on: vertical bars of varying height suggest sound in general, but this is not an established control convention a first-time user could map to one action; sitting beside a microphone it does not distinguish itself — my reading, confidence medium
screen1-a8.initial_rationale: no visible text, and the sound-bars glyph is not a recognizable convention; next to a microphone nothing says how it differs

test_cases.action: inspect the composer row for any caption, and type into the box to see whether the control changes or gains a label
test_cases.expected_result: no visible text in any state reached
test_cases.confirms_if: no caption appears in any state
test_cases.overturns_if: a caption or label appears in some state
test_cases.observed_result: no caption in any state; when text is typed the control is replaced by an orange send arrow, and when the box is empty it returns as the unlabeled bars glyph

test_cases.action: tap the bars glyph and observe what starts
test_cases.expected_result: if it is a recognizable convention, what starts would match it
test_cases.confirms_if: what starts does not match any reading of the glyph
test_cases.overturns_if: it behaves as a glyph a first-time user would predict
test_cases.observed_result: not run: this control starts a live spoken session, which this run does not permit on the devices

screen1-a8.deciding_evidence: verification found no visible text in any reachable state and the glyph is not a convention; the behavioural tap could not be run, so the verdict is provisional
screen1-a8.recommendation: add a visible label such as 'Talk' or 'Voice chat' under or beside the button, distinct from the microphone
